text:
Ana Patel: Quick heads-up — KV cache memory steadily grows on long contexts when running INT8-quantized variants. Ran a 250k-token tail workload and saw memory climb until eviction/paging kicked in. Profiling attached: https://artifacts.redwood/prof/1751203456 :warning:
Dmitri Ivanov: repro run? which model, batch config, and eviction policy?
Ana Patel: tiny-LM-13b-int8 on 4xA100, batch_size=1, streaming enabled, eviction_policy=lru, max_pages=2048. First message at top of thread has the raw profiler.
Kevin Zhao: hunch: kernel selection falling back to non-fused int8 attention kernel which spikes mem while converting back/forth. I saw similar when we missed the fused int8 matmul.
Ana Patel: that matches traces — see this snippet from the timeline:
```
KV_WRITE layer_10: alloc_page(16MB) -> copy (host->gpu) -> dequantize_fp16_path -> persist
ATTN_STEP layer_10: fallback_kernel=int8_deq_gemm (high temp buffers)
```

ml-bot: profiling-summary: total_kv_mem_by_layer = [layer0: 512MB, layer1: 496MB, ..., layer10: 648MB]; fragmentation_estimate=22%; page_flip_count=1873; host_pinned=1.6GB; device_kv_peak=38.9GB
Samira Khan: 22% fragmentation is... a lot. That explains why INT8 weight savings (40% lower) didn't translate to overall lower memory. Pages are aligned and small leftover fragments add up. :thinking:
Dmitri Ivanov: can you share delta vs FP16/BF16 runs? numbers matter for tradeoffs.
Ana Patel: FP16 run for same workload: device_kv_peak=35.1GB, fragmentation=12%, total_device_peak=62GB (weights+kv). INT8: weights down ~40% but device_kv_peak up ~10% due to extra staging buffers and page churn.
Kevin Zhao: so net device peak not improved much. Also we noticed a throughput regression in cold-cache scenarios: first-token latency +8-12% vs FP16 because of dequant sync points.
Zoe Rivera: are we doing dequant on write or read? If we dequant on write we pay once, but if writes are kept compressed and dequant on GPU read we can avoid repeated work but need a fast path for attention that reads INT8 directly.
Ana Patel: currently we dequant on write for compatibility with existing fused attention kernels (which expect FP16). That was a pragmatic choice when int8 kernels were immature.
Samira Khan: suggests trying generational eviction + compacting GC pass to reduce fragmentation. Idea: keep hot prefixes non-evictable for a window, evict cold pages in contiguous chunks to reduce page splits.
Dmitri Ivanov: yes — LRU causes scattering. Generational approach + buddy allocation for pages could reduce internal fragmentation overhead.
Kevin Zhao: also consider pointer-swapping for reuse: map host-backed contiguous buffer for KV and swap page pointers between device/host instead of memcpy when possible. That saved us 20-30% CPU time in previous on-prem tests.
Zoe Rivera: pointer-swapping requires pinned host pages or GPUDirect to avoid copies. We have limited pinned pages budget. We could implement a hybrid: small hot pages pinned; cold pages use async DMA.
Ana Patel: notes on accuracy: INT8 run had a small but measurable degradation on our eval suite — perplexity +0.8% and a 1.5% bump in factuality errors on long-context QA traces. Worth flagging.
Dmitri Ivanov: that aligns with quantization noise accumulating in KV cache for long contexts. Reuse of quantized KV across many steps can amplify small rounding errors.
Samira Khan: possible mitigations — stash FP16 for attention keys/values for top-N most recent layers while quantizing deeper layers; or mixed-precision KV: store index pointers + compressed int8 pages and maintain a small FP16 shadow of hot regions.
Kevin Zhao: mixed-precision shadow sounds promising. Cost model: shadowing top-4 layers FP16 adds ~6-8% memory but should recover most of the accuracy loss and reduce repeated dequant overhead.
ml-bot: eval-run-1751203456-int8-vs-fp16: ppl_fp16=11.06, ppl_int8=11.15, factual_err_fp16=3.2%, factual_err_int8=4.7% (long-context subset).
Zoe Rivera: another angle: implement layer-aware quantization scale per page. Instead of single global scale, use adaptive per-page scale and per-head centering to reduce dynamic range errors in KV entries. More metadata but less accuracy loss.
Ana Patel: agreed. But adding per-page metadata increases page header overhead; need to model trade-offs (header size vs reduced dequant expansion).
Dmitri Ivanov: re: perf regressions — primary culprit is kernel fallback. We should prioritize shipping fused int8 attention + kv-read path that consumes int8 directly. That eliminates dequant jitter and some temp buffers.
Kevin Zhao: I have a patch branch where int8 fused attention is used and we keep KV as int8 pages (no dequant on write). Early internal tests: device_peak down 9%, first-token latency improved vs the current int8 path, and no extra dequant copies. Will push for review.
Samira Khan: scheduling note: before landing, add a synthetic long-context stress test in perf-run CI that runs 1M token emulator with page churn to catch regressions.
Ana Patel: agreed. Also adding regression monitors on perplexity/factuality for our canonical long-context eval set and a mem-leak detector for kv-pages would help catch slow growth.
Zoe Rivera: final thought — we might also benefit from compacting allocator that runs during low-util windows to defragment. Combine with generational eviction and int8-fused kernels + mixed-precision shadowing — should get us good memory/accuracy balance.
Ana Patel: plan of action: 1) Kevin to open PR for fused int8 attention + keep KV int8 pages, 2) Dmitri/Samira to prototype generational eviction + compacting GC, 3) Zoe to prototype per-page adaptive scales + small FP16 shadow experiment, 4) add long-context perf/eval tests to CI. I'll consolidate tasks and create GH issues. :raised_hands:
Kevin Zhao: will open PR and include microbenchmarks.
Dmitri Ivanov: I'll prototype allocator change this week.
Samira Khan: I'll add the stress CI job and metrics.
ml-bot: note: created issue #2048 (kv-int8-fused-path) and #2049 (kv-allocator-gen-evict)
Ana Patel: thanks everyone. If you find more traces drop them here.
Kevin Zhao: one small repro command for reviewers:
```
python tools/run_long_context.py --model tiny-LM-13b-int8 --tokens 250000 --batch 1 --stream
```
Zoe Rivera: cheers.
Ana Patel: closing loop later today with a short writeup. :memo:"
